about.title: Rio Dell Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Rio Dell's small size doesn't mean workplace accidents don't happen — from timber-adjacent operations to retail, logistics, and roadwork crews along US-101 and SR-283, employees here face real risks on the job. When an injury happens at work, California generally routes claims through workers' compensation, which pays medical care and partial wage loss regardless of fault, but doesn't cover pain and suffering. If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured workers in Rio Dell with an independent attorney who can review the details of the incident, explain your options, and help you understand whether a third-party claim applies to your situation. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers money for you.

items.title: Third-Party Claims Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but if a negligent third party — like a subcontractor, driver, or equipment maker — contributed to your injury, a separate claim may be available. An attorney can help sort out whether that applies to your case.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim. An independent attorney can advise you on your rights if you're worried about your job.

items.title: Deadlines That Matter
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party injury claim carries a 2-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so timing matters.

items.question: I was hurt at work in Rio Dell — do I file a lawsuit or a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, meaning you generally can't sue them directly even if they were careless. However, if someone outside your employment — like a contractor, property owner, or another driver — contributed to your injury, a separate claim against that third party may be possible. An independent attorney can help you figure out which paths apply.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work near US-101 or SR-283 in Rio Dell?
items.answer: Work-related vehicle collisions, including those on corridors like US-101 near Davis Street or the SR-283 Eagle Prairie Bridge, can involve both workers' comp and a potential third-party claim if another driver was at fault. These cases often have more moving parts, so getting an attorney's read on the details can help clarify your options.

items.question: How long do I have to report my workplace injury?
items.answer: California law generally requires you to notify your employer within 30 days of a workplace injury to preserve your workers' comp rights. If a third party is involved, that separate claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Acting sooner rather than later helps protect all your options.
